questions.question: Who gave the 'General Equilibrium Theory'?
questions.solution:
Option **2** is correct, i.e __**Leon Walras**__.

__
 
• **First-time** general equilibrium formulated by French economist** ****Léon Walras**__.
 
• **General equilibrium theory**, or **Walrasian general equilibrium**, seeks to describe the workings of the macroeconomy as a whole, rather than assets of individual market anomalies.
 
• General Equilibrium Theory was first propounded by Leon Walrus in 1874.
 
• It attempts to explain that interaction of **demand and supply** will result in an overall general equilibrium.

**Extra information:**

 
• Born in 1723, **Adam Smith** is regarded as the **Father of Economics** due to his immense contribution to the subject.
 
• Amongst his many books, the most famous is the "W**ealth of Nations**" (1776) which is regarded as the first work in modern economics.
 
• Smith influenced many later thinkers such as Karl Marx, Joseph Schumpeter, **David Ricardo**, and many more.

questions.question: Which of the following carries oxygen to various parts of human body?
questions.solution:
​The correct answer is **Red blood cells.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] __Important Points__

__
 
• Red blood cells (Erythrocytes):

 
 
• RBCs are the biconcave cells without nuclei in humans; also known as erythrocytes.
 
• RBCs contain the iron-rich protein called hemoglobin.
 
• RBCs are the most copious blood cell produced in bone marrows.
 
• Their main function is to transport oxygen from and to various tissues and organs.
 
• Haemoglobin, aside from being a transport molecule, is a pigment.
 
• It gives the cells their red color (and their name).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__

 
• White blood cells (Leucocytes):

 
 
• ​Leucocytes are colorless blood cells.
 
• They are colorless because it is devoid of hemoglobin.
 
• They are further classified as granulocytes and agranulocytes.
 
• WBCs mainly contribute to immunity and defense mechanism.
 
 
 
• **Blood plasma** is a yellowish liquid component of blood that normally holds the blood cells in whole blood in suspension.
 
 
• It is the liquid part of the blood that carries cells and proteins throughout the body.

questions.question: Which of the following function is performed by the kidneys in the human body?
questions.solution:
Option **1** is correct, i.e. __**Excretion**__.

__Concept:__

__
 
• Kidneys are the excretory organs in the majority of mammals including humans.
 
• Kidneys regulate water and electrolyte balance (osmoregulation) along with the excretion of metabolic waste and foreign chemicals.
 
• Nephrons are the functional unit of kidneys.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• Kidneys perform a very crucial function of **excretion** in the human body.
 
• The main function of the** kidney is to purify the blood** that is present in the body and excrete waste in the form of urine. 
 
• A nephron is a functional and structural unit of the kidney (organ), which is involved in the process of excretion.
 
• It is made up of renal corpuscle or Bowman’s capsule, Glomerulus, Proximal Convoluted tubule, Loop of Henle, and Distal Convoluted Tubule.
 
• Bowman’s capsule is a double-walled cup-like structure in which the dense network of blood capillaries (Glomerulus) is present.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9a4c7a50c41ddac60a30271a51db3a176dbe5c6159b2778301a7f300bd117f89.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__

Respiration - 

 
• The breaking of the C-C bonds of complex compounds through oxidation within the cells, leading to the release of a considerable amount of energy is called respiration. 

Digestion - 

 
• The process of conversion of complex food substances to simple absorbable forms is called digestion and is carried out by our digestive system through mechanical and biochemical methods

**Transportation -**

 
• It is the movement of substances across the cell membrane either into or out of the cell.

questions.question: What is the reason for formation of Mirage in desert?

options.text: Both Refraction and Total internal reflection of light

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**option 3**__.

 
• The mirage is caused by the total internal reflection of light at layers of air of different densities.
 
• In a desert, the sand is very hot during day time and a result the layer of air in contact with it gets heated up and becomes lighter. The lighter air rises up and the denser air from above comes down.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/617fac791227b2b6687f6db273c983de14b28361b326a7938e20b22d1ea98c77.png] 

 
• As a result, the successive upper layers are denser than those below them. A ray of light coming from a distant object, like the top a tree, gets refracted from a denser to a rarer medium.
 
• Consequently, the refracted ray bends away from the normal until, at a particular layer, the light is incident at an angle greater than the critical angle.
 
• At this stage, the incident ray suffers total internal reflection and is reflected upwards.
 
• When this reflected beam of light enters the eyes of the observer, it appears as if an inverted image of the tree is seen and the sand looks like a pool of water.

 

So, Mirage is an example of total internal reflection which occurs due to atmospheric refraction.

questions.question: Which of the following bonds are weakest in nature?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Hydrogen bond.__

__Concept:__

Chemical bond:

__
 
• A chemical bond is a force or linkage which holds two or more atoms together in a stable molecule.
 
• The driving force for atoms to combine is related to their tendency to attain stable electronic configuration.
 
• A chemical bond may be formed either by electron transfer or electron sharing.
 
• 
 
Ionic Bonds:

 
 
• 
 
​Ionic bond formation occurs via electrostatic attraction between two ions.

 
 
• One ion is positively charged and the other is negatively charged like in NaCl.​
 
 
 
• Covalent bonds:
 
 
• Covalent bond formation occurs when there is electron sharing occurs between two atoms.
 
• The electron pair is shared equally between the atoms forming the bond-like in Cl2.
 
• When there exists a single bond between two atoms, there is only a sigma bond.
 
• When there exist multiple bonds between atoms, there is only one sigma bond and others are pi bond.
 
 

​Explanation:__

 
• Whether a bond is weak or strong depends on the extent of linkage or interaction among the molecules or atoms.
 
• Besides the chemical bond, there exist interactions between the molecules, which are not actual bonds, which means that there is no sharing or transfer of electrons but only interaction between the molecules is there.
 
• The types of interactions are:
 
 
• Electrostatic: They are interactions between charged molecules.
 
• Induction: These types of interactions arise when there is induction of dipole in the molecule.
 
• Dispersion: These are also called London forces or Van der Waals forces and exists mostly in covalent molecules.
 
• Hydrogen bonds: Hydrogen bonds are the dipole-dipole interactions that occur when a Hydrogen is bonded to a very electronegative atom like oxygen, Nitrogen. It is not a covalent bond.
 
 
 
• So, the Hydrogen bond is just an interaction between the Hydrogen and an electronegative element where there is no electron exchange leading to weak bonding between molecules whereas a single bond, double bond, and triple bond are covalent bonds and not just interactions.
 
• Chemical bonds are much much stronger than chemical interactions.
 
• It is difficult to break chemical bonds whereas Hydrogen bonds are easily and rapidly formed and broken under normal biological conditions.
 
• Hence, the bond strength order is: 

triple bond > double bond > single bond > H-Bond.

Hence, the weakest among the bonds is the Hydrogen bond.
